evidence_tree.limitation: The scenario roster definition for 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' lives outside the permitted export (it is not present anywhere under data/ or in docs/math-foundations.md). The reconstruction below therefore recovers the participant's max health and the exact amplification ratio from the two golden values themselves, then tests that ratio against the cached wiki effect text.

sources_quoted.quote: {{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
sources_quoted.reading: +7% damage taken, all damage types, but scoped to an ENEMY champion that the item holder has immobilized (and only that champion — 'marks them').

sources_quoted.quote: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.
sources_quoted.reading: +12% damage taken, MAGIC damage only, scoped to ENEMY champions inside a 700-unit aura around the holder. Never applies to the holder's own team, and never to physical or true damage.

sources_quoted.source: CLAUDE.md domain block, restated in docs/math-foundations.md §5 row 'Stat growth (growth_stat)'
sources_quoted.reading: used to invert the participant's max health from the two golden endpoints.

sources_quoted.quote: display-level integer rounding of health/AD/AP/armor/MR before damage
sources_quoted.reading: the participant's max health entering the damage walk is an INTEGER — this is what makes the inversion below identifiable rather than under-determined.

step_1_invert_max_health.method: Let H be participants[2] max health (an integer per the stat-rounding row). Damage taken is D_old = H − 438.6 and D_new = H − 686.2. Their ratio r(H) = (H−438.6)/(H−686.2) is the amplification the change removed. Because both endpoints are printed to 1 decimal, r is pinned to ±~1e-4, which is tight enough to be a real discriminator.
step_1_invert_max_health.search: Scanned every champion in data/champions.json at every level 6..20 (and separately with 1-3 health items added) for an integer H whose r(H) lands inside the rounding interval of a natural amplifier composition {1.07, 1.12, 1.07×1.12=1.1984, 1+0.07+0.12=1.19}.
step_1_invert_max_health.unique_no_item_hit: Exactly one champion/level with NO items fits any natural composition: Thresh at level 13, H = 1934.000 (exact integer, no rounding drift). r(1934) = 1495.4 / 1247.8 = 1.1984292, versus 1.07 × 1.12 = 1.1984 — agreement to 3e-5, inside the ±1e-4 print-rounding band.
step_1_invert_max_health.rejected_near_misses: Galio L18 (H=2742) gives r=1.120443 vs 1.12 — 4.4e-4 off, ~7× the rounding band, rejected. Belveth L20 (2743) r=1.12038, Gragas L19 (2746) r=1.12021, Garen L15 (1990) r=1.18991, Soraka L17 (1988) r=1.19020 — all outside their bands. No champion at any level reaches base health 2749/2750 or 4222–4224, so the 'curse only' and 'mandate only' readings require an item-loaded participant, whereas the 'both removed' reading closes on a bare champion.

step_2_closure.conclusion: The change removed, from participants[2]'s ENTIRE incoming-damage total, a multiplicative stack of Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable (×1.07) and Abyssal Mask's Curse (×1.12). Nothing else changed — the underlying un-amplified damage 1247.8 is identical on both sides.

step_3_rule_test.question: Does the cached wiki text license a flat ×1.07×1.12 on 100% of a roster participant's incoming damage?
step_3_rule_test.abyssal_mask: No, on two counts. (a) The curse is MAGIC-only: '12% increased magic damage'. Applying it to a participant's whole damage total is correct only in the degenerate case where every damage instance in the window is magic; any auto-attack, physical ability part, or true-damage part in that total is being amplified in violation of the quoted text. (b) The curse is scoped to 'Enemy champions within 700 units of YOU' — the holder's own team is never cursed.
step_3_rule_test.imperial_mandate: No. Vulnerable is a per-target MARK, not an aura: 'Immobilizing an enemy champion marks THEM as Vulnerable'. It attaches to the specific enemy the holder immobilized. Blanketing it across the roster (or onto the holder's own side) has no support in the text.
step_3_rule_test.therefore: The old value required participants[2] to satisfy, simultaneously, every one of: enemy of the Abyssal holder, inside the 700-unit aura, immobilized by the Mandate holder, and taking exclusively magic damage. The new value requires only that participants[2] falls outside the scope of both effects — which is the default for an ally/holder-side participant, for a secondary enemy that was never immobilized, and for any participant whose incoming damage is not magic. Every scoping rule quoted above cuts in the direction the change went (fewer amplifiers), and none cuts back.

alternative_readings_considered.reading: participants[2] is an item-loaded participant with H=2749/2750; the change removed only Abyssal's ×1.12 (Vulnerable's ×1.07 retained).
alternative_readings_considered.status: possible but a worse numeric fit (all candidate champion+item healths sit 3–7 rounding-widths off 1.12); verdict direction is UNCHANGED — removing a magic-only curse from non-magic damage is still the wiki-faithful move.

alternative_readings_considered.reading: participants[2] has H≈4223; the change removed only Mandate's ×1.07 (Curse retained).
alternative_readings_considered.status: possible; again the verdict direction is UNCHANGED — un-blanketing a single-target immobilize mark is wiki-faithful.

alternative_readings_considered.reading: The correct answer is a partial amplifier — e.g. curse-only on a secondary enemy hit exclusively by magic AoE, giving ending_health = 536.5 (or mandate-only, 598.9). That would make BOTH endpoints wrong.
alternative_readings_considered.status: cannot be excluded from the permitted export, because the roster's damage-type mix is not recoverable from data/. It is not asserted here: it requires positive evidence that exactly one of the two effects legitimately reaches participants[2], and no such evidence exists in the cached wiki text. Flagged as the residual risk on this verdict.

alternative_readings_considered.reading: The +247.6 is an added shield/heal rather than a removed amplifier.
alternative_readings_considered.status: rejected — it would be a coincidence that H−686.2 multiplied by exactly (1.07)(1.12), the product of the two amplifiers named in the scenario id, reproduces H−438.6 to the printed decimal.

confidence: high on the mechanism (the 1.07×1.12 closure is exact to the printed precision and the max health inverts to a bare champion at an exact integer), medium-high on the verdict (the scenario roster is outside the permitted evidence tree, so 'both_wrong' via a partial amplifier cannot be formally excluded)
